cards.note: Hat - Austria, Bulgaria, Czechia, Slovakia. > those with Horizontal Crosswalk - Austria.
Horizontal Zebra stripe: Austria, Belgium, Greece, Poland, Serbia. > LEGO MAN: Belgium.
White Belt: Croatia/Bosnia, Portugal, Germany, Hungary. > Non-Pointed Shoes: Croatia/Bosnia, Portugal. > Straight legs: Croatia/Bosnia.
Hat - Austria, Bulgaria, Czechia, Slovakia. > those with 4 Zebra Stripes: Bulgaria.
White Belt: Croatia/Bosnia, Portugal, Germany, Hungary. > Non-Pointed Shoes: Croatia/Bosnia, Portugal. > Straight legs: Croatia/Bosnia.

Hat - Austria, Bulgaria, Czechia, Slovakia. > Those with 5 Zebra Stripes: Czechia, Slovakia. > Extra blue border on edge and Tucked-in shirt: Czechia. White border on edge and Draping jacket at waist: Slovakia.
Denmark's guy has a chill walking posture and has rounded edges on the person. Often found on thicker, 3D blue squares. His arms are also pointed down, unlike some similar signs found in Scandinavia.
3 Zebra Stripes: Estonia, Lithuania, Russia, Ukraine. Neck / Shoes / Detailed outline is unique to Estonia.

Detailed man without a hat and 5 Zebra stripes is Finland. Features both the detailed man's outline and the bold rounded, non-detailed person. Finland's bold non-detailed man with 5 zebra stripes has one arm pointed up, unlike Denmark.

Has 2 designs, one of them has no bent elbow on the left arm which is unique to France. The other is the standard Italy-styled one, but French pedestrian signs all share a fat white border not found elsewhere.

White Belt: Croatia, Portugal, Germany, Hungary. > Pointed Shoes: Germany, Hungary. > Germany Belt: Above hip. Hungary Belt: Bottom of hip. Germany arm: Flat side on left. Hungary arm: Flat side on right.

Horizontal Zebra stripe: Austria, Belgium, Greece, Poland, Serbia. > Detailed guy with no hat: Greece. Note that Greece's icon has hair that may almost look like a hat but it's just hair. Kinda looks like the Dame Tu Cosita guy

White Belt: Croatia, Portugal, Germany, Hungary. > Pointed Shoes: Germany, Hungary. > Germany Belt: Above hip. Hungary Belt: Bottom of hip. Germany arm: Flat side on left. Hungary arm: Flat side on right.
Iceland is the only sign with a yellow triangle instead of white.
Italy, Romania, Serbia, and Slovenia all look about the same. Thankfully Romania will not have a white/silver border. Italy will have blue corners visible outside the white edge.
You can identify Latvia from their guy with weirdly long legs. Long as hell for what. It's arguable Russia/Ukraine/Lithuania has long legs but even so they have 3 zebra stripes, not 5.

3 Zebra Stripes: Estonia, Lithuania, Russia, Ukraine. > Cross off Estonia and Russia (detailed guy in Estonia, Yellow borders in Russia) and you're left with Lithuania and Ukraine. Lithuania's guy is a liiittle bit more fat in the torso than Ukraine and the blue is generally more vibrant than Ukraine.
Netherlands' guy has funny limbs, they shrink towards the end sorta like a starfish.
4 Zebra Stripes: Norway, Sweden, Bulgaria. > Bold, non-detailed person: only Norway.
Horizontal Zebra stripe: Austria, Belgium, Greece, Poland, Serbia. > Single & continuous line: Only Poland.
White Belt: Croatia/Bosnia, Portugal, Germany, Hungary. > Non-Pointed Shoes: Croatia/Bosnia, Portugal. Bent knees: Portugal.
Italy, Romania, Serbia, and Slovenia all look about the same. Thankfully Romania will not have a white/silver border.
3 Zebra Stripes: Estonia, Lithuania, Russia, Ukraine. > Russia is the only one with yellow borders.

Serbia has 2 different pedestrian signs. Horizontal Zebra stripe: Austria, Belgium, Greece, Poland, Serbia. > No hat + rounded, non-detailed guy: Serbia. OR 5 Zebra stripes + rounded guy + no belt + white/silver border + no blue corners: Serbia, and Slovenia.

Hat - Austria, Bulgaria, Czechia, Slovakia. > Those with 5 Zebra Stripes: Czechia, Slovakia. > Extra blue border on edge and Tucked-in shirt: Czechia. White border on edge and Draping jacket at waist: Slovakia.
Italy, Romania, Serbia, and Slovenia all look about the same. Thankfully Romania will not have a white/silver border. Italy will have blue corners visible outside the white edge.
Spain has a whopping 8 zebra stripes.
4 Zebra Stripes: Norway, Sweden, Bulgaria. > Detailed man without a hat: only Sweden. Personally I easily identify Sweden from the gyatt
Turkey's sign has extra blue space above the triangle compared to the rest.

3 Zebra Stripes: Estonia, Lithuania, Russia, Ukraine. > Cross off Estonia and Russia (detailed guy in Estonia, Yellow borders in Russia) and you're left with Lithuania and Ukraine. Lithuania's guy is a liiittle bit more fat in the torso than Ukraine and the blue is generally more vibrant than Ukraine.
